verdict.rationale: Token2's own documentation shows its FIDO keys use an on-device PIN: browsers prompt to set one, and Token2's companion app and fido2-manage tool can set and change it and enforce a minimum PIN length. The tooling also manages biometric templates, but it is manufacturer-agnostic, so this does not confirm biometric hardware on Token2 keys. missing for 10: explicit documentation that user verification is enforced so a stolen key cannot authenticate, confirmation of built-in biometric sensors on Token2 keys, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the key supports on-device user verification — a FIDO2 PIN or built-in biometric — so a stolen key alone cannot authenticate
